selected.title: He Let His Brother Move In Without Asking Me
selected.hook: My boyfriend promised his brother he could move into our apartment for three months without asking me.
selected.voiceover:
My boyfriend promised his brother he could move into our apartment for three months without asking me.

We'd been living together for almost a year, and his brother had just lost his lease. I knew he was having a rough time, so when my boyfriend said he might need help, I assumed we were going to talk about options.

Then I got home Friday and there were boxes in our hallway.

His brother was carrying in a suitcase.

I asked what was happening, and my boyfriend said, "He's staying with us for a while."

A while meant three months.

They had already agreed on it two days earlier.

Our apartment has one bedroom, I work from home three days a week, and the couch is basically in the same room as my desk.

I asked why nobody thought to mention this before the boxes arrived.

My boyfriend said his brother is family and shouldn't need an invitation when he's struggling.

I said helping family is one thing. Volunteering our shared home without asking me is another.

Then he accused me of making his brother feel unwelcome, even though I never said he couldn't stay. I just wanted us to decide together how long, where he'd sleep, and what the plan was.

Now his family thinks I'm selfish.

If you share a home with your partner, can either person promise someone a place to live without asking first?
selected.youtube_description:
She knew her boyfriend's brother needed help, but she didn't expect to come home to boxes already moving into their one-bedroom apartment. Her boyfriend had promised him three months without asking first. Is helping family automatic, or does a shared home require two yeses?
